title: Best Practices for Spirituality and Religion in Counseling: A Review of its Development and Implications
abstract: Abstract The Association for Spiritual, Ethical, and Religious Values in Counseling ( aservic ) last published competencies for addressing spiritual and religious issues in counseling in 2009. This article describes the 2025 revision, which reframes these competencies as best practices. Key structural changes include reorganization from six categories into the Ways Paradigm (i.e., Ways of Being, Ways of Understanding, and Ways of Intervening ), an intentional shift in terminology, and explicit integration of cultural humility and intersectionality throughout the framework. The revised best practices approach emphasizes ongoing professional development rather than fixed achievement, which reflects spirituality and religion as dynamic dimensions of human experiences. Supplemental documents include reflection questions, a resource guide, and guidance to support practical implementation. Implications for counselor education, supervision, and professional development emphasize holistic integration rather than checklist approaches. This revision positions counseling professionals to more effectively address spiritual and religious considerations in culturally responsive and ethically informed ways.
